# Agency

`customer_support.offering.service.agency` · offering_type · parent `customer_support.offering.service`

> Ongoing creative and campaign execution on retainer — marketing, design, content, media. Two structural facts make this type unlike its siblings. The first is that the deliverable is subjective and revision is the normal mode of work. A client saying "this is not right" is not reporting a defect; it is the process functioning as designed. Support-shaped thinking fails immediately here, because the concept of a correct output that can be verified does not exist — there is only agreement, and agreement is reached by iterating. The genuine failure mode is not a wrong deliverable but an unbounded number of revisions, which is why scope is measured in rounds rather than in tickets. The second is that the clock is external and unforgiving. Campaigns launch on dates set by media buys, seasons, product launches and events that will not move. A missed deadline is not a late ticket, it is a paid placement running with the wrong creative, and it cannot be recovered by working faster afterwards. Urgency in this type is almost entirely calendar-driven and almost never severity-driven. A third, quieter fact: the client contact is usually a marketer being judged internally on the work we produce. Their escalations are frequently about their own exposure rather than about the deliverable, and reading them as quality complaints produces confidently wrong responses. The habit carried in from professional services and punished here is treating a revision request as a change request. Some are; most are the work.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| delivery | continuous creative output against a retainer, delivered in rounds and agreed rather than verified |
| pricing_shape | monthly retainer sized to a volume of work, plus project fees and pass-through media spend |
| margin_profile | bounded by utilisation and destroyed by revision creep; the difference between a profitable and unprofitable account is usually rounds, not rates |
| post_sale_load | the whole engagement is post-sale load, delivered continuously with no terminal state |
| support_load | calendar-shaped and deadline-clustered. Contact rate spikes before every launch and in the hours after anything goes live, and is near zero in between |
| resolution_locus | a human redoing creative work. There is no fix, only another round, and every round consumes margin that cannot be recovered |
| notes | Revisions are the unit that matters. An account can look healthy on every satisfaction measure and be losing money purely on round count, and round count appears in no standard support metric.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.entitlement`

Requires `plan`, `coverage_hours`


> Entitlement here is the retainer, and the unit it bounds is rounds of revision rather than hours or incidents. An agency that cannot answer "how many rounds does this account get" at ticket time will discover the answer in the margin report, and by then the precedent is set.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.commitment`

Requires `promised_at`, `due_at`, `owner_ref`


> Deadlines here are external and irreversible. A missed commitment means a placement runs with the wrong creative, which cannot be fixed by delivering later — so this object carries more consequence in this type than an SLA does anywhere in the tree.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.customer_sentiment`

Requires `trajectory`


> Dissatisfaction in an agency relationship is expressed as increasing revision demands long before it is expressed as a complaint. Trajectory across rounds is the leading indicator; the complaint, when it comes, is a lagging one.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Deactivating knowledge_authoring is the arguable call. Agencies do maintain brand guidelines, tone-of-voice documents and asset libraries, and those are genuine reusable knowledge — but they are client-owned deliverables produced by the creative team, not support knowledge produced to reduce contacts. Modelling them here would put the support function in charge of an artefact it does not author and cannot maintain.
